land.text: Cliopatria's 540 shape of Glywysing, cut out of the sub-Roman Brythonic lands: south Wales between the Neath and the Rhymney

predecessors.note: The Glywysing page's infobox has the kingdom form after the Roman withdrawal, in the late 5th century, and the lands lie between the Afon Llwyd and the Loughor or the Neath; the Morgannwg page gives no formation date. 540 is Cliopatria's start.

land.text: the lowlands of Glamorgan (the Vale), parcelled out to Robert Fitzhamon's followers as the Lordship of Glamorgan

successors.note: Iestyn page: Iestyn was deposed c. 1090 by Robert Fitzhamon; 'The mountainous parts of Glamorgan were left in Welsh control' and Caradog ap Iestyn kept the land between the Neath and the Afon (the lords of Afan). Cliopatria's Norman England row (1085-1093, 182,668 km2) borders it.

capitals.name: Cardiff
capitals.note: Infobox of the Glywysing page: capital Cardiff; the Morgannwg page names none.

region.text: Glywysing, south Wales between the Neath and the Rhymney

ledger.note: 540: Morgannwg (Glywysing) is on the map. The Morgannwg page says only that south-east Wales was a kingdom called Gwent in the early 9th century, later split into Glywysing in the west and Gwent in the east, and that the name Morgannwg came into use at the end of the tenth century; the Glywysing page puts the formation in the late 5th century with Glywys c. 470-c. 480. 540 is Cliopatria's start (page silent).

942: Morgan Hen unites Gwent and Glywysing as Morgannwg. The page: he united Gwent and Glywysing in 942 under the name Morgannwg, or Gwlad Morgan; the infobox gives the union as 942-974. Cliopatria draws the union from 947 to 959.
975: Gwent is separate from Morgannwg again. The page: the kingdoms separated again after Morgan Hen's death in 974. Cliopatria draws the separation in 960.

1055: Gruffydd ap Llywelyn conquers Morgannwg. The page: he conquered both Gwent and Glywysing in about 1055; the Gruffydd page has him seize Morgannwg and Gwent around the same time he recaptured Deheubarth in 1055.
1063: the native line regains Glywysing. The page: on Gruffydd's death in 1063 the native line under Caradog ap Gruffudd regained Glywysing.

1074: Caradog unites Gwent with Morgannwg. The infobox has the union 1063-1074 and the name Morgannwg from 1075 under Caradog ap Gruffydd; the Gwent page (second page) has Caradog take control of what remained of Gwent from Cadwgan in 1074.

region.text: Gwent, the lordships of Caerleon, Monmouth, Striguil, Abergavenny and Usk

ledger.note: 1086: the Normans hold Gwent. The page: they established a castle at Caerleon by 1086 and extinguished the Kingdom of Gwent; the Gwent page (second page) has most of Gwent firmly under Norman control when Caradog died in 1081. Striguil castle stood by 1071.

region.text: Morgannwg (Glywysing): the Vale of Glamorgan lowlands

ledger.note: c. 1090: Robert Fitzhamon deposes Iestyn ap Gwrgant and the Normans take Glamorgan. The Iestyn page: he was 'deposed c. 1090 by Norman ruler Robert Fitzhamon', the lowlands were parcelled out to Fitzhamon's followers and the mountains left in Welsh control (the lords of Afan); the Morgannwg page has the conquest 'around 1091' and the Glywysing ruler list ends Iestyn in 1091.

wars.name: Gruffydd ap Llywelyn's conquest of Wales
wars.outcome: Gruffydd conquered Gwent and Glywysing in about 1055 and held them until his death in 1063, when the native line under Caradog ap Gruffudd regained Glywysing.
wars.note: The Gruffydd ap Llywelyn page does not say that native rulers regained Morgannwg after 1063.

wars.name: Norman invasion of south-east Wales
wars.outcome: The Normans reached Striguil by 1071 and Caerleon by 1086, extinguishing the Kingdom of Gwent; the attacks faltered after Roger de Breteuil forfeited his estates in 1075.
wars.note: The page is silent on Robert Fitzhamon, Glamorgan and Iestyn ap Gwrgant.

wars.name: Norman conquest of Glamorgan

zones.text: the Vale of Glamorgan, parcelled out to Fitzhamon's followers

wars.outcome: Robert Fitzhamon deposed Iestyn ap Gwrgant c. 1090; the lowlands became the Lordship of Glamorgan, the mountains stayed Welsh.
wars.note: Popular version: Iestyn invited Fitzhamon and twelve knights in to settle a dispute with Einion ap Collwyn and 'Once invited in, they refused to leave'. The page gives no year for the division.

certainty.note: The pages say the borders of Glywysing were uncertain and changed over time; no treaty or survey line is given.

notes: Cliopatria ends Morgannwg in 1055 (Gruffydd ap Llywelyn); the Glywysing page has the native line back in 1063 and the Iestyn page has Iestyn deposed c. 1090, so the dossier runs to 1090 with new keyframes for 1063-1073, 1074-1085 and 1086-1089. End year: the Iestyn page says c. 1090 and 1081-1093 in its infobox, the Glywysing page 1081-1090 in its text and 1091 in its ruler list, the Morgannwg page 'around 1091'; 1090 is the Iestyn page's. The Glywysing infobox gives the Gwent union as 1063-1074 and Morgannwg from 1075, while its ruler list gives Caradog 1063-1081. Disagreement with the Gwent dossier: the Gwent page has an independent Gwent 1063-1074 and the Glywysing page a union 1063-1074; this dossier follows the Gwent page for the dates and holds Gwent from 1074 to 1085. The Morgannwg page is a stub: it gives no formation date, no area and no capital. The Glywysing ruler list is partial (c. 470-580, c. 755-785 and c. 840-974, then 1055-1091) and was not turned into a ruler strip. Pages silent: Robert Fitzhamon's invasion year and the division of Glamorgan (Iestyn page), Brycheiniog, the Viking raids, Wessex and Mercia; Morgan Hen's 931 submission to Athelstan is on the Morgan Hen page opened for the Gwent dossier (a vassal event for the England dossier). Gwynllwg went to Owain ap Caradog, founder of the Lords of Caerleon (Glywysing page, no date). Counterparts needing dossiers: marcher-lordships (the Lordship of Glamorgan and the Welsh uplands of Afan). Gazetteer: Glywysing, Gwynllwg and Afan are not in the gazetteer; regions here are Cliopatria shapes and Vale of Glamorgan.
